relevance_note: The paper is a case report of SSADH deficiency: "Genetic testing revealed a homozygous mutation in the aldehyde dehydrogenase 5 family member A1 (ALDH5A1) gene", and it describes the infant, her mother and her sibling, but no TNFAIP3 variant is mentioned anywhere.
method_note: Read the full text by hand; no script transcribed any table. This paper has no tables, so no stacked cells. The paper reports no cohort and states no total number of patients, so publications.cohort_size_as_stated is null (the only count given, "approximately 450 patients reported worldwide", is about SSADH deficiency worldwide, not this study). Individuals: the single unnamed patient of the case report (label 'patient'), her mother, and her sibling who died at one year without genetic testing ("Genetic testing was ordered for her at that time but unfortunately was not done due to financial reasons"); the sibling therefore gets no variants row. The father is mentioned only as one of "Her parents" ("Her parents were first-degree cousins") with no other individual-level fact, so I gave him no row; this is the main judgement call. Consanguinity 'yes' is recorded for the patient and for the sibling, who had the same parents. The one printed variant is the patient's "homozygous mutation G->A substitution at chr6:24505155"; the paper prints no cDNA or protein HGVS, and no variant type, zygosity word beyond 'homozygous', pathogenicity classification or ACMG criteria, so those fields are 'not reported' rather than derived from the HGVS-like string. 'homozygous' is taken from the authors' phrase 'homozygous mutation', which describes this patient's variant. The sentence 'Akaboshi et al. predicted this mutation to cause an abnormal protein translation' is recorded under functional_evidence_statement as a prediction, not an assay result. No parental testing for the variant is reported, so inheritance is 'not reported'. Death: vital_status 'deceased' for the patient, cause 'respiratory failure' as stated in the case narrative (the abstract's phrase is 'leading to fatality'); her age at death is recorded as P4M only because the paper calls her a "four-month-old female infant" and she died during the same admission, and the same span supports age_at_last_evaluation P4M. No HPO identifiers are given because I was not sure of them. Contradictions: none found.
